purpose: VESPA provides seven C++ command-line (CLI) modules for 3D Slicer that perform surface-mesh processing and repair (alpha wrapping, boolean operations, isotropic remeshing, subdivision, hole filling, mesh repair, and shape smoothing) on VTK polydata models. It is intended for Slicer users who need robust CGAL-based polygon mesh processing algorithms wrapped via Kitware's VESPA VTK filters.
summary:
VESPA is a well-structured C++ SuperBuild extension by Kitware that exposes seven CGAL/VESPA surface-mesh processing algorithms as standalone CLI executables (`EXECUTABLE_ONLY`). All external dependencies in the SuperBuild are pinned by SHA256 hash (Boost, CGAL, Eigen3) or commit hash (Kitware's VESPA repository), and no Python environment modifications or network operations occur at runtime. Licensing is permissive (3-clause BSD) for the source code, with clear disclosure in `CMakeLists.txt` and `README.md` that the compiled CLI executables are governed by GPLv3 due to CGAL.

🟢 Recommend merge

safety.rationale: Inspected all 19 text files in the repository, including all C++ sources and CMake superbuild scripts. External tarballs (Boost 1.86.0, CGAL 6.0.1, Eigen 3.4.0) are pinned with SHA256 hashes from official URLs, `vespa` is pinned to a specific commit on `gitlab.kitware.com`, and the CLI code only reads input `.vtp` meshes, processes them in memory with VTK/CGAL, and writes output `.vtp` files.

environment.rationale: Inspected all CMake and C++ files (`CMakeLists.txt`, `SuperBuild.cmake`, `SuperBuild/*.cmake`, `SlicerVESPA/*`). The extension builds standalone C++ CLI executables (`EXECUTABLE_ONLY`) with static VESPA libraries and header-only Boost, CGAL, and Eigen3, without modifying Slicer's Python environment or global process state.

packaging.rationale: Inspected the catalog entry, `CMakeLists.txt`, `SuperBuild.cmake`, `SuperBuild/*.cmake`, and `SlicerVESPA/CMakeLists.txt`. `build_subdirectory` matches `EXTENSION_BUILD_SUBDIRECTORY` (`inner-build`), `build_dependencies` matches `EXTENSION_DEPENDS` (`NA`), and all seven CLI modules have matching `.cxx` and `.xml` files configured via `SEMMacroBuildCLI`.

license.rationale: Inspected `LICENSE.txt`, `CMakeLists.txt`, and `README.md`. The extension source is under a 3-clause BSD license (`LICENSE.txt`), and the authors clearly document that the CLI modules are built as separate-process executables (`EXECUTABLE_ONLY`) whose distributed binaries are governed by GPLv3 due to linking CGAL's GPLv3 packages.

soundness.rationale: Inspected `SlicerVESPA/*.cxx`, `SlicerVESPA/vespaRepairMesh.h`, and `SlicerVESPA/*.xml`. The C++ CLI modules properly validate inputs, catch `std::exception` during CGAL mesh repair, handle non-manifold and self-intersecting meshes before boolean corefinement, and run out-of-process as standard Slicer CLI executables.

utility.rationale: Inspected `README.md`, `CMakeLists.txt`, and all module `.xml` descriptors. The extension provides well-documented surface mesh processing tools (including 3D Alpha Wrapping and CGAL corefinement boolean operations with automatic soup/self-intersection repair) that complement Slicer's existing surface model tools.

findings.title: CLI XML metadata lists LGPL instead of BSD-3-Clause / GPLv3
findings.explanation: Each CLI XML descriptor declares `<license>LGPL</license>`, whereas `CMakeLists.txt` (lines 12) and `README.md` (lines 65-69) explicitly note that the CGAL algorithms used here (such as Polygon Mesh Processing and 3D Alpha Wrapping) are licensed under GPLv3+, making the resulting CLI binaries governed by GPLv3, while the extension source itself is 3-clause BSD (`LICENSE.txt`). This metadata mismatch in the CLI XML descriptors could confuse users inspecting the module help panel.
findings.suggestion: Update `<license>` in the seven `.xml` files to `BSD-3-Clause (source) / GPL-3.0-or-later (binary)` or `GPLv3` to match `README.md` and `CMakeLists.txt`.

findings.title: No automated tests included for the CLI modules
findings.explanation: The repository does not define automated CTest tests for the seven CLI modules. Adding simple baseline CLI invocation tests would help catch regressions on the Slicer build farm.
findings.suggestion: Consider adding `BUILD_TESTING` checks and basic `sem_add_test` / CTest tests for the CLI modules.

not_checked: The external VESPA repository source code at https://gitlab.kitware.com/vtk/meshing/vespa.git (commit c1f3bc913767c206d3a9665faea9aa24774262bb) fetched during the superbuild could not be inspected directly in this environment.
